record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.original_question: For bounded operators, were the following two equivalent assertions true: first, if T:L1(0,1)->L1(0,1) is bounded and T restricted to every subspace M isometric to ell_1 is an isomorphism, then T is an isomorphism; second, if T:ell_infty->ell_infty is bounded and has dense range, then T is surjective?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Are the following two assertions, which are equivalent, both true?

(A) Every bounded linear operator $T:L_1(0,1)\to L_1(0,1)$ with the property that the restriction $T|_M$ is an isomorphism onto its image for every closed subspace $M\subset L_1(0,1)$ that is isometric to $\ell_1$ is itself an isomorphism onto its image.

(B) Every bounded linear operator $T:\ell_\infty\to\ell_\infty$ with dense range is surjective.

Here $L_1(0,1)$ denotes the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue integrable real-valued functions on $(0,1)$ with the $L_1$-norm, $\ell_1$ is the Banach space of absolutely summable real sequences, $\ell_\infty$ is the Banach space of bounded real sequences with the supremum norm, and "isomorphism" means a bounded linear bijection with bounded inverse (onto its image, i.e., a linear homeomorphic embedding).
artifact.status_search_result: The equivalent assertions were given a negative answer in 2013, around the time of the Castro Urdiales 2014 problem list. A bounded operator on $\ell_\infty$ with dense but non-closed range was constructed, equivalently giving a non-isomorphic operator on $L_1(0,1)$ that is an isomorphism on every isometric copy of $\ell_1$.
